reasons: Classification as a deviation is correct: Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and (via the broad 'Derivative Work' definition at 1.3) in any additions, enhancements or customizations in Licensor, the 'Intellectual Property Rights' definition is drafted as rights 'of Licensor' only, and nothing in the Agreement confirms Licensee retains its data or pre-existing IP. The clause therefore fails not only the preferred position but also the fallback, since Licensee gets no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the work product it funds under Article VII(b) — only a term-limited, field-of-use-limited licence renewable at Licensor's option.

Redline is minimal and directionally correct: it leaves Licensor's ownership of its platform intact (expressly permitted by the rule), adds a Customer Data / pre-existing IP retention sentence with no-assignment and no-joint-ownership language, and assigns paid-for customizations to Licensee with a licence-back for embedded Licensor IP — exactly the drafting the redline guidance calls for, appended as a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' carve-out rather than rewriting the clause.

Comment is accurate, uses the [Playbook] prefix and first person plural, explains what changed and why in two sentences, and offers the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the customizations) if ownership is resisted.
Deterministic checks pass; no over-flagging (the clause is not already at the fallback) and no duplication with another rule.
